Thank you for taking the time to share your thoughts regarding the proposed Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) trade agreement. I appreciate hearing from you and welcome the opportunity to respond. Like you, I want to grow the economy and create more jobs for North Carolina and for the country. I support free trade because it promotes innovation and encourages competition, which lead to more and better-paying jobs and better selection of products at a lower cost to American consumers. In addition to the economic growth within the United States, free trade fosters relationships and ensures our national security. Robust trading partners almost never go to war.

While TPP, in concept, presents an opportunity for North Carolina to increase its exports and boost the economy, any trade agreement signed by the United States must be fair for both sides to ensure the protection of North Carolina's economy and jobs. The details of the draft TPP text are available for review in a secure facility in the Capitol, and I have personally read the proposal. I have concerns with several provisions that I will be closely monitoring as negotiations continue.

Once negotiations are completed, Congress will have up to four months to review the text before a vote is taken to accept or reject the trade agreement. There will be an additional 60 days for public comment before the president can sign any trade agreement. When TPP comes before the Senate, I will carefully consider everything you have said in making a decision on what is best for North Carolina and the rest of the country.

Again, thank you for taking the time to contact me. It is important to hear from citizens on issues that affect the state and the nation. Please do not hesitate to get in touch with me again about other important issues.
